title: Egress: why reading can cost more than storing

videos.script: Most people price a bucket by its size. That is one meter of four, and often the smallest. {{meters}} Every request has a price, whatever it carries. Listing a prefix is billed like a write. The colder classes charge again for reading. And every byte that leaves has a price too. {{classes}} In this lesson you count requests yourself, from the emulator's own log. Twenty taps uploaded one by one are twenty-one billed requests. Packed into one file, they are two. {{count}} Then a short program prices it at Quitanda's size. Two million taps read every morning spend over a hundred times their storage on requests. {{small}} Then the product images, served to the internet. The transfer is nearly the whole bill, and a cache in front of the bucket takes a third of it off. {{tiers}} Then the traffic that stays inside Google Cloud. Same region is free. From São Paulo, any other region costs the same high price. And a NAT gateway charges for the bucket next door. {{inside}} Last, Requester Pays, the setting that sends the bill to whoever asks. {{payer}}
